rounds.response:
Analysis: Opposing Counsel’s concessions on a 5‑month window, rolling productions, and reduced depositions are reasonable starting points we can accept only if we preserve (1) the ability to take up to eight fact depositions per side, (2) a phased expert schedule that allows liability experts to proceed (no blanket stay), and (3) each party’s right to bring targeted early motions after substantial completion of core document production and depositions; we should politely but firmly decline any proposal that locks the entire case schedule to their contemplated motion.  

Proposed discovery framework to circulate (language you can copy/adapt): Fact discovery 5 months from initial disclosures with rolling productions beginning 30 days after disclosures; initial “core” production (schedules, change orders, payment records, key custodial ESI and related communications) to be substantially completed within 90 days and prioritized; up to eight fact depositions per side (meet‑and‑confer to resolve scope/custodian disputes); expert discovery phased—not stayed: liability expert disclosures due 30 days after substantial completion of fact discovery, rebuttals 30 days thereafter, with damages/valuation experts to follow or as the Court orders; either party may seek targeted, discrete dispositive or Daubert relief after substantial completion of core production and depositions with an agreed short briefing schedule or submit dates to the Court.  

26(f) talking points: (a) No blanket stay of expert discovery—phased expert timing protects proportionality while avoiding prejudice and permits efficient testing of liability issues; (b) We won’t agree to hard‑wire the case timetable around their anticipated motion—we’re open to discussing genuinely narrow early motions but need flexibility to file targeted motions where our record supports them; (c) Concede efficiency measures (rolling productions, custodian lists, agreed search terms, prompt ESI meet‑and‑confer) to show good faith and narrow disputes.
